correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs both signed proximal resolvents mode by mode. With symmetric endpoints, the source weights give the exact positive Hessian eigenvalue h(lambda)=lambda^2/((Lambda_+-lambda)(Lambda_-+lambda)). Pairing the positive and negative endpoint modes yields the stated strict lower bound on the merit condition number. The infimum follows by sending both regularization parameters to infinity. The fixed-step factor is the exact two-endpoint minimax factor for an SPD quadratic. A packaged standard-library replay checks representative parameters; the proof, not the finite replay, covers all quantified parameters.

value.rationale: The result isolates a concrete mechanism behind the gap between the new merit-based upper scale and the better class-level information benchmark: the entire admissible two-parameter paired-Moreau family has a kappa-squared conditioning floor on the smallest balanced indefinite endpoint witness. The statement is exact, sharp in the parameter limit, and identifies acceleration or preconditioning of the merit—not retuning the two Moreau parameters—as the mathematically relevant direction if one seeks to beat this outer fixed-step barrier.
